simple.meaning: תֹּקֶף (tôqeph) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “might or (figuratively) positiveness.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Esther, Daniel, beginning at Esther 9:29. Its contexts include family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תֹּקֶף (H8633).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: תֹּקֶף (tôqeph) / H8633 is traced through Esther 9:29, Esther 10:2, Daniel 11:17 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H8633. toqeph תֹּ֫קֶף noun masculine power, strength, energy (Aramaic תֹּקֶף תְּקוֺף, ); — ׳ת absolute Est 9:29 ; construct Dan 11:17 , the strength of his whole kingdom ; suffix תָּקְמּוֺ Est 10:2 the deeds of his power (+ גְּבוּרָתוֺ , etc.).

occurrences.englishText: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.

All the acts of his power and of his might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, to which the king advanced him, aren’t they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?

He will set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and with him equitable conditions. He will perform them. He will give him the daughter of women, to corrupt her; but she will not stand, and won’t be for him.
